label: Who's Who & Your Legal Status
labelZh: 校園組織與你的法律身分
blurb: Who does what, and what your contract and visa depend on.
blurbZh: 誰負責什麼，以及你的合約與簽證繫於哪個處室。

questions.stem: You need a copy of your contract, a leave form, and confirmation that your health insurance is active. Which office do you go to?
options: 總務處 Office of General Affairs
學務處 Office of Student Affairs
教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
人事室 Personnel Office
questions.why: The 人事室 holds your contract, leave records, insurance enrollment and work-permit paperwork. In a small school this may be one person, sometimes combined with 會計室 / 主計室. Learn their name in your first week — they will handle more of your life in Taiwan than anyone else at the school.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: Your timetable has changed, you need to know which textbook a class is using, and you want to book the English classroom. Which office?
options: 學務處 Office of Student Affairs
教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
輔導室 Counseling Office
人事室 Personnel Office
questions.why: 教務處 owns curriculum, timetables, textbooks, exams and room assignment. The person you will deal with most is the 教學組長 (Curriculum Section Chief).
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: A student is injured during your class, and separately you want to know why the whole school is outside on Wednesday morning. Which office covers both?
options: 教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
總務處 Office of General Affairs
會計室 Accounting Office
學務處 Office of Student Affairs
questions.why: 學務處 covers student safety, health (健康中心 and the school nurse), discipline (生教組), clubs and assemblies. Injuries, fights and anything about student behavior outside the classroom go here.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: A student in your class has stopped speaking, seems withdrawn, and a Taiwanese colleague mentions 「家裡的狀況」— the situation at home. Which office is the right one to raise this with?
options: 教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
總務處 Office of General Affairs
輔導室 Counseling Office
人事室 Personnel Office
questions.why: 輔導室 handles student counseling, special educational needs and referrals to social services. Raising a concern here is always appropriate and is never overreacting. Note: if you ever suspect abuse or neglect, a legal 24-hour reporting duty applies — that is Module 4 in December.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: The projector in your classroom is broken and you have lost your classroom key. Which office?
options: 學務處 Office of Student Affairs
教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
總務處 Office of General Affairs
輔導室 Counseling Office
questions.why: 總務處 handles buildings, equipment, keys, repairs and purchasing. The 事務組 inside it is your practical contact.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: In a Taiwanese elementary school, which single person usually knows the most about an individual student's academic level, family situation, friendships and health?
options: The Principal 校長
The homeroom teacher 導師
The Director of Academic Affairs 教務主任
The English subject teacher
questions.why: The 導師 stays with the same class for years, eats lunch with them, supervises cleaning time, and is the family's main contact. For almost any student-level question — behavior, absence, a note from home — the 導師 is your first stop, before any office.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: Which description of school job titles is correct?
options: 主任 = section chief; 組長 = director
主任 = director of an office; 組長 = section chief within that office
主任 and 組長 both mean principal
組長 is used only for administrative clerks
questions.why: The hierarchy runs 校長 (Principal) → 主任 (Director, heads a 處/室) → 組長 (Section Chief, heads a 組 inside it) → 老師 (teacher). Addressing someone as 王主任 or 李組長 shows you understand the structure — but calling any of them 老師 is never wrong or rude.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: Your work permit as a foreign teacher at a public school is tied to a specific employer. A nearby cram school (補習班) offers you six well-paid hours on Saturdays. What is the legal position?
options: Fine, because it is outside your contracted school hours
Fine as long as your principal gives verbal permission
Illegal unless a separate permit is obtained for that employer — a fine of NT$30,000–150,000 and possible loss of your right to stay
Fine as long as you pay tax on the extra income
questions.why: Under the Employment Service Act a foreign national may not work without a permit for that specific work and employer. Article 68 sets a fine of NT$30,000–150,000, and the authorities may revoke the permit and order departure. Your principal cannot authorize this — only the competent authority can. This is the single most common way a foreign teacher loses their position in Taiwan.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: You move to a new apartment in November. What must you do about your ARC (外僑居留證)?
options: Apply to change your registered address at a National Immigration Agency service center within 30 days
Nothing until the ARC is renewed
Tell your school only — the school will handle it
Nothing; the ARC address is not required to be current
questions.why: Your ARC address must be kept current with the 內政部移民署, within 30 days of the move. An out-of-date address causes real problems later — renewal, tax documents and official mail all go to the registered address. Tell your Personnel Office too, but the legal filing is yours.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: When does your National Health Insurance (健保) coverage as a school employee begin?
options: After six months of residence in Taiwan
Only after you apply in person at an NHI office
From your first day of employment — your employer enrolls you
Only after your ARC has been valid for one year
questions.why: As an employed person you are enrolled by the school from your start date, with premiums deducted from salary. You will receive a 健保卡 — carry it; it is what makes a clinic visit cost a few hundred NT dollars instead of several thousand. A spouse and children living in Taiwan can usually be enrolled as dependents; ask Personnel.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: In Taiwanese income tax, what does the 183-day rule determine?
options: How long you may stay in Taiwan on one ARC
When you become eligible for National Health Insurance
Whether you are taxed as a resident at progressive rates, or have the higher non-resident flat rate withheld from your salary
When you may apply for permanent residence
questions.why: 183 days or more within a single calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec) makes you a tax resident, filing an annual return at progressive rates. Under 183 days in that calendar year, salary is subject to non-resident withholding at a higher flat rate. This matters most in your first and last partial years. The annual filing period is 1–31 May, for the previous calendar year.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: A typhoon is approaching. Who decides whether your school closes tomorrow?
options: Your principal
The Ministry of Education
Each teacher decides individually
The county or city government — for you, the Changhua County Government
questions.why: Closure (停止上班上課) is announced by the local government, usually the evening before or by about 5:00 a.m. Check the Changhua County Government announcement or local news, not just your school's LINE group. If the county announces closure you do not go in, and you are not expected to work from home unless your contract says so.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: You wake up with a fever and cannot teach today. What is the correct first action?
options: Follow the leave procedure in your contract — notify Personnel and your co-teacher before the school day starts, and submit the leave form
Post in the school LINE group and wait to see if someone replies
Message your students' parents directly
Simply do not attend; sick days do not need advance notice
questions.why: Foreign English teachers are employed under a contract, not under the Teachers' Act, so your leave entitlement and procedure come from your contract and your school's rules — not from the regulations governing Taiwanese certified teachers. The number of days, the notice period and the form differ between schools, so confirm the exact procedure with Personnel in Week 1. Notifying early matters: someone has to cover your classes.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: Which hotline should a foreign resident call for 24-hour English-language help with everyday life in Taiwan — visas, health insurance, housing, general questions?
questions.why: 1990 is the Foreigners in Taiwan hotline: free, 24 hours, in English, Japanese, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Thai. Learn the others too — 110 police, 119 fire and ambulance, 113 Protection Hotline for child abuse, domestic violence and sexual assault (English available; you will use this in Module 4), 1957 social welfare.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: You see a sign on an office door reading 學務處. What is inside?
options: Student Affairs
General Affairs
Academic Affairs
Personnel
questions.why: 學 = study/student, 務 = affairs, 處 = office. Its neighbour 教務處 (教 = teaching) is Academic Affairs. Reading these five signs is the fastest way to stop needing a guide around your own school.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: The school calendar (行事曆) tells you all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Exam weeks
Which textbook each grade is using
Make-up school days that fall on Saturdays
Sports day and the school anniversary
questions.why: The 行事曆 is the single most useful document you will receive all year. Ask 教務處 for a copy in Week 1 and put every date in your phone — especially the make-up school days (補課日), which are working Saturdays that compensate for extended holidays. Textbooks come from 教務處 separately.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: 朝會 refers to:
options: A parent-teacher conference
A staff meeting held after school
A whole-school morning assembly, often outdoors, with announcements and sometimes a flag-raising ceremony
The morning cleaning period
questions.why: 朝 = morning, 會 = gathering. Ask your co-teacher which mornings it runs and whether foreign teachers are expected to attend and stand with a class — practice varies between schools, and simply showing up the first time is the easiest way to find out.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: After lunch in most Taiwanese elementary and junior high schools, the lights go off and students rest at their desks. This is:
options: An optional break students may skip
A period reserved for make-up lessons
Unsupervised free time
午休 — a scheduled quiet/nap period, part of the school day
questions.why: 午休 is normally 20–40 minutes, supervised by the homeroom teacher, and is treated as part of the school day. Do not schedule activities, meetings or noisy preparation during it, and do not read a sleeping class as a discipline problem.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: 打掃時間 (cleaning time) means:
options: Students clean their own classrooms and assigned areas of the school as part of the daily timetable
A punishment assigned to misbehaving students
Cleaning staff clean the school while students are in class
An optional after-school volunteer activity
questions.why: Students cleaning the school is standard practice and is treated as part of their education — not as labour and not as punishment. If your class has an assigned area you may be asked to supervise. Joining in occasionally, even briefly, is noticed and appreciated far out of proportion to the effort.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: A well-known cram school offers you Saturday work. The owner says: “Many foreign teachers here do this. Your school will never know, and we have never had a problem.” Your best response is:
options: Accept — the risk appears to be low in practice
Decline, unless a separate work permit is obtained for that employer — the exposure is a fine and loss of your right to stay, and it is enforced
Accept, and declare the income in May to make it legitimate
Accept, but ask your principal for verbal permission first
questions.why: “Everyone does it” and “nobody checks” are not defences. Declaring the income does not cure the permit problem — the offense is working without authorization for that employer, not failing to pay tax. Your principal has no power to waive it. Enforcement is usually triggered by something unrelated: a labour inspection, a dispute with the cram school, or an ARC renewal.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: A parent finds you on LINE and adds you directly, then asks detailed questions about their child's progress — and about another student in the class. The most appropriate response is:
options: Ignore the messages entirely
Block the parent without explanation
Answer fully; good parent communication is part of the job
Reply politely, decline to discuss any other student, redirect substantive matters to the homeroom teacher, and tell your co-teacher the contact happened
questions.why: Two separate issues. Discussing a different student's behavior or performance with a parent is a privacy problem — that is Module 7 in April. And in Taiwanese schools the 導師 is the designated channel to families; going around them creates confusion and undercuts them. Keeping your co-teacher informed protects you both: never let them hear about a parent contact from the parent.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: It is March. You are fairly sure you want to return next year, but nobody has said anything about renewal. What should you do?
options: Wait — the school will raise it when they are ready
Wait until June, closer to the contract expiry
Assume renewal is automatic unless told otherwise
Raise it yourself with Personnel and the principal, because staffing plans and budget cycles are decided months before the school year ends
questions.why: Schools plan headcount, funding applications and recruitment well before the year ends. Silence is not a signal about your performance — it usually means nobody thought to tell the foreign teacher about a process conducted in Chinese. Asking early is not pushy; it is what a returning colleague is expected to do. Ask specifically about the timeline, the paperwork, and whether your work permit and ARC renew in step with the contract.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: At 8:10 a.m. your co-teacher asks you to cover her 8:40 class — she has been called into a meeting. You have never taught that class and have no materials. The best response is:
options: Agree if you reasonably can, ask what the class is working on and whether the homeroom teacher will be there — and raise the pattern with her later if it becomes frequent
Agree, and use the time for unplanned free talk
Refuse; covering another teacher's class is outside your contract
Agree, then report the request to Personnel
questions.why: Short-notice cover is normal and reciprocal in Taiwanese schools, and saying yes builds real goodwill. But “yes now” and “let's talk about this” later is a legitimate combination. Raise the pattern directly and privately with your co-teacher first — going to an office before speaking to the person concerned makes her lose face and will damage the working relationship far more than the original request did.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分

questions.stem: You are leaving Taiwan at the end of June and will not return. Which of these is most likely to be forgotten and to cause a real problem?
options: Settling your tax before departure, and closing out NHI, pension and ARC obligations in the right order
Saying goodbye to your classes
Handing over your teaching materials
Returning your classroom keys
questions.why: A departing resident generally must settle income tax for the current year before leaving rather than waiting for the following May, and there are separate steps for NHI withdrawal, any pension or severance entitlement under your contract, closing a bank account, and surrendering or letting the ARC lapse. Start this with Personnel six weeks before departure, not in the final week. Doing it badly can cause problems if you ever apply to work in Taiwan again.
questions.mz: 校園組織與你的法律身分
